raw.details:
NEXORA ’26 is a technology-driven project-building event designed to bring together creative minds, developers, innovators, and problem solvers to transform real-world challenges into practical technological solutions.

The event provides participants with an opportunity to identify a problem, develop an innovative solution, build a working prototype, and present it before a panel of judges.

Whether you are a solo developer or part of a small team, NEXORA ’26 gives you a platform to showcase your technical skills, creativity, problem-solving ability, innovation, and presentation skills.

Participants will receive a problem statement and will be given a limited time to conceptualize, develop, and submit their solution. The event will conclude with a short project presentation and Q&A session before the judges.

Objectives:

NEXORA ’26 aims to:

  • Encourage students to develop innovative technological solutions.
  • Promote practical problem-solving and creative thinking.
  • Provide hands-on experience in project development.
  • Encourage collaboration and teamwork.
  • Help participants transform ideas into working prototypes.
  • Provide a platform to showcase technical and presentation skills.
  • Encourage the development of solutions for real-world problems.

Who Can Participate?

The event is open to all types of students who are interested. The age of the participants must be above 17:

Registration is limited to 50 teams. Secure your spot before the slots fill up!

Participants can register:

  • Individually, or
  • As a team of 2–3 members

Maximum Event Capacity: 50 teams

First come, first served

Registration Fee:

  • Individual Entry: ₹100
  • Team Entry (2–3 Members): ₹200

There will be no cash refund policy available

Prize Pool:

The best 3 teams will be awarded with the cash prize.

How the Event Works

  • Registration: Participants register individually or as a team.
  • Inauguration & Briefing: The event begins with the inauguration ceremony, followed by the rules briefing and problem statement announcement.
  • Problem Statement: Teams receive the problem statement and understand the requirements before beginning development.
  • Project Building:
    • Participants work on their solution within the allotted development time.
    • Teams can use appropriate development tools, frameworks, libraries, and permitted online resources. There will be 3 hours provide for the project making
  • Submission:
    • Teams must submit their final project as link before the announced submission deadline.
    • Once the project is submitted, no changes will be allowed.
  • Evaluation: Submitted projects will be evaluated by the judges based on predefined evaluation criteria.
  • Presentation & Q&A
    • Each team will get:
      • 2 Minutes — Project Presentation
      • 1 Minute — Q&A Session
      • Total: 3 Minutes per Team
  • Results & Prize Distribution: The winners will be announced after the evaluation process, followed by prize distribution.
  • Presentation Format
    • Each team must present their project within 2 minutes.
    • Participants are recommended to cover:
      • Problem identified
      • Proposed solution
      • Key features
      • Technology used
  • The presentation will be followed by a 1-minute Question & Answer session.
  • Teams exceeding the allotted time may be stopped by the coordinators.

Important Rules & Instructions

  • Team size must be 1–3 members.
  • The participants will be allowed to make the projects for 3 hours
  • There must bring their own internet connectivity.
  • Participants must follow the given problem statement.
  • The project must be developed within the allotted time.
  • Original work is required.
  • Plagiarism, copying, or unfair practices are strictly prohibited.
  • Teams may use appropriate development tools and permitted online resources.
  • Participants are responsible for their own laptops, chargers, and required development resources.
  • The final project/link must be submitted before the announced deadline.
  • No changes will be allowed after final submission.
  • Participants must verify their project and submitted link before final submission.
  • Each team gets 2 minutes for presentation + 1 minute for Q&A.
  • The total presentation and Q&A time is 3 minutes per team.
  • Participants must maintain discipline and professional behaviour throughout the event.
  • Teams must follow instructions given by the event coordinators and judges.
  • Any violation of the rules may result in disqualification.
  • The coordinators' decision will be final.

What Participants Should Bring

Participants are advised to bring:

  • Laptop
  • Laptop charger
  • Required development software/tools
  • Internet connectivity
  • college ID
  • Any additional resources required for project development
